transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-31 15:00 UTC | Duration 62m | Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Lena (Evergreen ML Ops), Marcus (CTO), Priya (Infra)

Summary: (auto) Focused on POC scoping for cost modeling + unit economics. Discussed traffic shape, target p95 latency, budget, and benchmark plan. Next steps agreed.

00:00 Sophie: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
00:07 Marcus: yeah Marcus Reed CTO, hi. lena and priya here as well.
00:12 Lena: hi, Lena. main ask is we want to understand per inference cost under our typical load and how batching or prefix caching could change that.
00:20 Sophie: perfect. marco and i will run through the baseline model and cost assumptions - then we can get to benchmarks.
00:28 Marco: quick note, our model of interest is a 8k context open variant, we'll probably run a quantized 4-bit for dedicated runs, hosted will use our standard validated shard.
00:38 Priya: can you explain the difference in real dollars and latency between hosted and dedicated? we're sensitive to p95 latency and monthly budget caps.
00:46 Marco: sure. rough ballpark: hosted per-token (inference) is $0.000025/token for generation tokens at our mid tier - that's without dedicated commit. Dedicated amortizes hardware so effective per-token can go down to ~$0.000012/token depending on utilization and batching.
01:00 Marcus: those are helpful numbers. what assumptions are on tokens per request? our median prompt is 120 tokens in, 240 tokens out.
01:08 Lena: yes about median 120 in / 240 out; tail up to 2k for some long manifests.
01:15 Marco: okay so baseline request ~360 tokens total. at hosted rate $0.000025 that's about $0.009 per request - hm math.. yes roughly $0.009. With dedicated and good batching we often see 30-50% cost savings; with caching/prefix KV on repeated prefixes maybe additional 20-40% depending on reuse.
01:33 Priya: caching? can you detail how prefix/KV cache reduces cost and latency? we have many repeated shipping descriptions.
01:40 Marco: sure. prefix caching stores KV cache for common prefixes so subsequent requests reuse earlier key-value states, cutting compute for the repeated prefix. For many enterprise patterns with repeated prompts, we've measured 30-60% token compute drop on average for high reuse. Also reduces p95 significantly.
01:55 Marcus: latency numbers - what p95 can we expect hosted vs dedicated with batching?
02:00 Marco: hosted typical p95 for this profile is 150-300ms depending on load; dedicated with local GPUs and lower busy factor can hit 80-180ms p95. If you push batching to increase throughput latency can go up a bit but cost per token drops. We can tune batching windows to hit your SLA.
02:20 Sophie: we should capture success criteria - what will Evergreen consider a pass?
02:24 Lena: success = p95 latency < 200ms for 90% of traffic, monthly inference cost below $X (they will send budget after call), and model outputs meeting our quality threshold (we'll supply eval set).
02:36 Marcus: also must pass security checklist: VPC peering, KMS for keys, SOC2 docs.
02:42 Priya: yes, and we have some data residency rules for EU shipments.
02:47 Marco: noted. we'll send SOC2 and network diagram. hosted can support region routing; dedicated gives more isolation.
03:00 Sophie: about the pilot length - we suggest 4 weeks of benchmark + small production-like traffic, then review. timeline?
03:06 Lena: that sounds good, we want internal stakeholders looped in after first week of bench.
03:10 Marco: for the bench we'll need: sample 1 week of traffic, token histogram (percentiles), canonical prompt list, and expected QPS.
03:18 Priya: currently average qps ~8, peak around 65, sustained peaks of 40 for short bursts.
03:24 Marco: good. for sizing dedicated, we'd model a baseline pool that supports 50 qps at 200ms p95 with scaling for peaks. If you want near-zero cold-starts and consistent p95 we'd recommend dedicated.
03:36 Marcus: and what's the delta in cost to reserve dedicated for a month vs burst on hosted?
03:41 Marco: depends on commitment. example: dedicated monthly commit might be $12k/mo for the minimal pool for your load, amortized gives lower per-token compared to hosted at scale. Hosted is pay-as-you-go so if usage is spiky might be cheaper short term. We'll put exact numbers in the POC spreadsheet.
03:58 Sophie: can we talk about optimizations: quantization, kernel selection and batching knobs you mentioned?
04:04 Marco: quantization to 4-bit typically reduces memory and increases throughput with small quality tradeoffs; for embeddings/generation we test accuracy on your eval set. Kernel selection and runtime choose optimal attention kernels for sequence length; batching we expose target batch size and latency ceiling. In the cost model we'll show tradeoffs: cost per request vs p95.
04:26 Lena: what's a reasonable expectation of cost reduction if we enable caching and moderate batching?
04:30 Marco: conservative estimate is ~35% reduction; aggressive reuse scenarios can reach 50-60%. We'll model low/medium/high reuse cases.
04:40 Priya: how do you simulate our traffic for benchmarks? do you need VPC access?
04:44 Marco: two options: run synthetic load from our test harness that mimics your token distribution, or run in your environment with VPC peering for live traffic. For security reasons many enterprises prefer the latter for fidelity, but it needs network setup.
04:58 Marcus: we'll likely start synthetic, then do a short live run.
05:02 Sophie: any blockers around encryption/key mgmt?
05:05 Priya: we require KMS integration and audit logs.
05:07 Marco: Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs in both hosted (with customer-managed keys) and Private/Dedicated. We'll include specifics in the docs.
05:16 Lena: ok, let's capture the exact success criteria now - p95 < 200ms for 90% traffic, monthly inference cost target (we'll send budget), quality pass on eval set >= 95% pass threshold (we'll send the eval cases).
05:29 Sophie: great. For the POC we'll propose: Week 0: kickoff + env setup; Week 1: synthetic benchmark with baseline config; Week 2: caching + batching experiments; Week 3: dedicated small pool run (if approved); Week 4: analysis and decision. Does that work?
05:47 Marcus: yes, and decision meeting with execs at end of Week 4.
05:51 Marco: i'll prepare the benchmark harness and share a runbook. we'll also provide sample quantization profiles to test.
05:59 Priya: on network, we'll draft peering steps, but initial synthetic runs will be fine.
06:05 Sophie: ok recap next steps: send POC pricing sheet, benchmark prompts, SOC2 and network docs, and set kickoff date.
06:14 Lena: thanks all. one more question - how do you present per-token cost given caching which reduces compute but not tokens?
06:21 Marco: good question. we present three metrics: nominal per-token list price; effective compute-cost-per-request after caching & batching; and cost normalized per useful token (i.e., tokens that actually required compute). That helps you compare to baseline.
06:36 Marcus: sounds sensible. can you include a sensitivity table showing cost vs reuse% and batch sizes?
06:41 Marco: yup we'll include low/med/high reuse scenarios and batch windows (10ms/50ms/100ms) and p95 tradeoffs.
06:50 Sophie: any competitive concerns? Lena?
06:52 Lena: we also spoke to TupleAI but they don't have dedicated runtime options for our scale. CloudServe was cheaper but had worse p95 in their benchmarks.
06:59 Sophie: ok we'll play to Redwood's strengths - unified runtime, observability, and predictable economics.
07:05 Marcus: one last thing - procurement timeline?
07:08 Lena: if POC looks good we aim to sign pilot contract within 6-8 weeks post decision.
07:12 Sophie: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
07:18 Call ends.
